definitions.explanation: A rapid, preliminary report of an event, especially in news media. Emphasizes speed of delivery over completeness of information.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}の{速報|そくほう}が{流|なが}れた。
{選挙|せんきょ}{速報|そくほう}を{見|み}ながら{結果|けっか}を{待|ま}った。
examples.english: I waited for the results while watching the election flash reports.

examples.japanese: ニュース{速報|そくほう}によると、{大型|おおがた}の{台風|たいふう}が{接近|せっきん}しているとのことだ。
examples.english: According to the news bulletin, a large typhoon is approaching.

notes:
A compound of {速|そく} (fast) + {報|ほう} (report). Commonly seen on TV and smartphone notifications for urgent news.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ニュース{速報|そくほう} (news flash)
- {地震|じしん}{速報|そくほう} (earthquake bulletin)
- {選挙|せんきょ}{速報|そくほう} (election flash report)
- {速報|そくほう}が{入|はい}る (a bulletin comes in)
- {速報|そくほう}{値|ち} (preliminary figures)

In Japan, {緊急地震速報|きんきゅうじしんそくほう} (Emergency Earthquake Early Warning) is a well-known system that sends alerts to phones before shaking arrives.
